Public servants were told to remove patients from elective surgery lists without confirming they no longer needed their operations, an ACT Legislative Assembly committee has been told.

Login or signup to continue reading

Independent MLA Thomas Emerson used parliamentary privilege to raise allegations from an anonymous whistleblower during a hearing about Canberra Health Services and Health and Community Service Directorate annual reports.

"I have been contacted by a whistleblower with serious allegations about the indiscriminate removal of patients from Canberra Health Services elective surgery wait lists," Mr Emerson said.

"[This included] surgical clerks being instructed to remove all patients who have been on the waitlist for over 500 days without consultation with their referring doctor and sometimes without even informing the patient they'd been removed.

"I'm told this instruction was given solely to improve the average wait time figures for elective surgeries, that staff were threatened with losing their jobs if they didn't comply and that their superiors refused to put these instructions in writing."

Canberra Health Services chief executive Janet Zagari said she was concerned about the allegation and promised an internal audit of waiting list management practices. Executives would also consider whether a report should be made to the ACT Integrity Commission.

"I'm not aware of any instruction of the nature that you've described and would be extremely concerned that if that were the case," Ms Zagari said.

Mr Emerson said patients had been removed from elective surgery waiting lists after missing two phone calls within a matter of minutes and letters to patients had been binned without being sent.

"I understand surgical booking clerks are required to attempt to contact a patient twice before they can be removed from a wait list on the basis of them being uncontactable," he said.

"So clerks have been told to call patients by phone and if the call is missed to immediately call them back again so they can be removed from the wait list."

Health Minister Dr Marisa Paterson said she was unaware of the allegations but they would be investigated.
